purpose: How an operator of a pest-control sales or referral business decides where to sell, whom to sell to and at what pace, by treating route density and the drive time hidden inside it as the governing cost mechanism of a recurring service account, choosing between running an own licensed operation and selling for a licensed operator, running door, referral and partner channels inside regulated-sales and disclosure-first constraints, and timing all of it against seasonal pest-pressure waves and the serviceable capacity of a technician-day.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

pesticide application is performed only by a person and business holding the applicable structural pest control operator and applicator credentials; this knowledge base addresses the sales and territory side of the business and never contemplates unlicensed application

the seller either runs a licensed operation or sells accounts serviced by a licensed operator under a written agreement, and can obtain that agreement's territory, account-ownership and compensation exhibits to read

solicitation permits, do-not-knock registries, home-solicitation cooling-off duties, sales-representative registration and pest-control licensing classes vary by jurisdiction and change over time, so every regulatory statement here names a class of obligation to verify with the applicable authority rather than asserting a current rule

every money quantity - service price, initial service fee, commission basis, clawback window, cost per stop, account payback - is treated as a mechanism with named drivers and a per-deal verification path, never as a stated figure
service is delivered on a route by a technician whose working day is bounded by time, so capacity is counted in stops and minutes rather than in dollars

this knowledge base is educational and operational for the seller or operator; it is not personalized legal, tax, financial or employment-classification advice, and it is not a pest diagnosis for any specific property
exclusions: the licensing and certification requirement classes for operators and applicators, the structure and drafting of the partnering agreement with a licensed operator, service-protocol literacy such as inspection method, treatment classes and prevention framing, and label-law and safety practice - that is the service delivery and licensing awareness knowledge base this one hands off to

service-agreement mechanics such as quarterly or monthly term, billing and renewal wording, retention practice, ethical cancellation-save conversations, seasonal add-on selling of mosquito, rodent or termite-inspection classes, and valuing an assembled account book as an asset - that is the recurring contracts and retention knowledge base
performing, directing or specifying any pesticide application, product, rate, dilution or label interpretation
diagnosing an infestation at a specific property, and in particular any wood-destroying-organism finding, which is a licensed inspection judgement referred out rather than asserted by a seller

asserting the current solicitation-permit, do-not-knock, cooling-off, sales-representative-registration or pest-control-licensing rule of any named jurisdiction; obligations are named as classes to verify with the applicable regulator and counsel

quoting any specific service price, initial-service fee, commission rate, clawback window, cost per mile, account multiple or market size as a fact; every such quantity appears only as a mechanism with its drivers and a verification path
personalized legal, tax, financial, insurance or worker-classification advice to a seller, operator, technician or customer
technician recruiting, training, payroll, chemical procurement and fleet operations, which enter here only as the capacity ceiling they impose on the rate of selling

competency_questions.question: Should I run my own licensed operation or sell accounts for a licensed operator, and what does each choice do to who owns the account and how I actually get paid?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OPERATING_MODEL_CHOICE states both model shapes with who bears service cost, who owns the account and who controls quality; REVENUE_MECHANISM_MAP names each revenue line and the document that proves it; COMMISSION_AND_CLAWBACK_MECHANICS states basis, vesting and reversal without quoting a rate

competency_questions.question: Why does route density decide whether an account makes money, and how do I turn drive time into a cost number I can actually use?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ROUTE_DENSITY_PRINCIPLE states that price is flat across geography while cost to serve is not, and DRIVE_TIME_COST_MECHANISM decomposes a stop into service minutes, travel minutes and dead time measured from real route data

competency_questions.question: How many accounts can one technician-day actually hold in this territory, and what is the scarce resource each sale consumes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ROUTE_DAY_CAPACITY_MODEL converts working minutes into stops per day and then into accounts supported at a service frequency, with assumptions stated as bands; SERVICE_TERRITORY_GEOMETRY supplies the zone the model is computed for

competency_questions.question: Which neighborhoods should I work first, and what evidence tells me a subdivision has genuine recurring pest pressure and reachable buyers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PEST_PRESSURE_GEOGRAPHY names the habitat, structural and land-use drivers read in the field; NEIGHBORHOOD_SEGMENT_SELECTION produces a ranked target list with a stated reason per neighborhood and excludes protected-characteristic targeting

competency_questions.question: How do I open a brand-new area without wrecking the density I already have, and how do I know when the new zone is genuinely open?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TERRITORY_SEEDING_AND_FILL requires an anchor, a bounded seeding period and concentric fill measured by penetration; DENSITY_SCORECARD_AND_ZONE_DECISION supplies the deepen-versus-open test and the exit condition for seeding

competency_questions.question: A prospect well outside my cluster wants service - do I take the account, price it for distance, park it on a waitlist or refer it away?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DENSITY_DILUTION_TEST gives the ordered test (anchor, cluster, absorbable by schedule, honestly priced for distance, otherwise park or refer) and requires the decision and reason to be recorded; INBOUND_DEMAND_CAPTURE explains why inbound leads arrive density-blind

competency_questions.question: What must I check and respect before knocking a single door in a neighborhood, and how do I keep that check current?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DOOR_SALES_REGULATORY_SCREEN names the obligation classes - permit and registration, hours, do-not-knock registries and posted signage, private community rules, home-solicitation cooling-off notice, follow-up contact rules - and produces a dated per-municipality checklist with a verify-locally instruction rather than asserted rules

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DOOR_CONVERSATION_CRAFT gives the identify-disclose-permission-show-leave sequence and bans urgency and fear closes; FINDINGS_EVIDENCE_DISCIPLINE separates conducive conditions, observed activity and licensed diagnosis; SALE_PROMISE_RECORD_HANDOFF lists what the handoff record must carry

competency_questions.question: How do I handle a household where consent may not be informed, or where health, pet, pollinator or garden sensitivities change what may be promised?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VULNERABLE_OCCUPANT_SAFEGUARDS states the stop-the-sale triggers for capacity and comprehension, the sensitivity classes to elicit and record, and the rule that the seller routes such questions to the licensed operator rather than answering them

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AUTHORITY_TO_AUTHORIZE_CHECK enumerates the tenant, household member, property manager, HOA, commercial-lease and transaction cases, gives the plain questions to ask, and requires written confirmation from the authority holder before proceeding

competency_questions.question: How is my commission constructed, when does it vest, what can claw it back, and how does that structure change which accounts are worth selling?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMMISSION_AND_CLAWBACK_MECHANICS names basis, vesting event, clawback condition and recovery method, residual treatment on termination, and states which selling behaviour each structure rewards

competency_questions.question: How should my selling volume, message and mix change across the pest-pressure seasons without overselling what can be serviced?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEASONAL_DEMAND_WAVE describes pressure classes as qualitative waves to verify against local observation and states the first-year service-event consequence of sale timing; SALES_PACING_TO_SERVICE_CAPACITY caps the sold-not-yet-serviced backlog against remaining route-days

competency_questions.question: Which acquisition channels build density fastest, and what disclosure do referral and partner arrangements require?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NEIGHBOR_REFERRAL_ENGINE explains why customer referrals are geographically adjacent and requires incentive disclosure to both sides and privacy of the referrer's own service details; PARTNER_REFERRAL_NETWORK covers portfolio, transaction and trade sources with the referral-compensation verification class and the capacity warning

glossary.definition: The number of serviceable accounts inside a small radius that one technician can work in a single route-day; the governing economic variable of this business, because the recurring price is roughly flat across geography while the time cost of reaching a customer is not.

The travel minutes between stops that a customer never pays for directly; the hidden unit cost of a scattered account, measured from real route timestamps at the hour the route actually runs rather than from off-peak map estimates.

One technician's working day assigned to one zone; the scarce resource every sale consumes, expressed as a number of stops after start-up, re-stock, access and callback time are removed from the working minutes.
One visit to one serviced property, costing on-site service minutes plus the travel minutes to reach it plus any access or waiting dead time; capacity, pricing and density are all counted in stops.
The share of doors in a target block or subdivision that are live accounts; the progress measure for filling a zone and the signal that decides whether to keep deepening or open new geography.

The first account or cluster in a new area that justifies the drive on its own - typically a property-manager portfolio, an HOA-referred group or a commercial account - around which concentric fill is built.

Visible, non-diagnostic property conditions that invite pest pressure, such as mulch against siding, wood-to-soil contact, standing water, dense harborage and gaps at weep holes or door sweeps; they may be shown and discussed by a seller, unlike a diagnosis.

A return visit between scheduled services under the service guarantee; cheap as a short detour inside a dense cluster and margin-destroying for an isolated account, which is why the guarantee's cost is a density question.

The period after a sale during which cancellation, non-payment or an unauthorized sale reverses the seller's commission; its length and recovery method are read from the compensation exhibit, never assumed, and it is the mechanism that makes account persistence the seller's problem.

A municipal list of addresses that have opted out of door-to-door solicitation, sitting alongside posted no-soliciting signage and private community rules; where such a registry exists its addresses are removed from the canvass plan before a route is walked, and its existence and weight must be checked per municipality.

nodes.definition: Decide, before any prospecting begins, which of the two money models this business runs on, and write down the consequences that follow from the choice. In the own-operation model the business holds - or employs the holder of - the applicable structural pest control credentials, carries the truck, the materials, the insurance and the technician minutes, keeps the whole recurring service fee, and owns the customer relationship as a transferable asset. In the sell-for-operator model the business generates and closes accounts that a licensed operator services, is paid a commission or a share defined by a written agreement, carries almost no service cost, and frequently does not own the serviced account at all unless the agreement grants that explicitly. The choice determines who bears service cost and liability, who controls the service quality that decides whether accounts survive, who owns the book, whether territory is exclusive or shared with other sellers, and which obligations attach to the seller personally rather than to the operator. Treat it as a document exercise rather than a preference: the operator agreement's territory clause, account-ownership clause, compensation exhibit, quality and complaint provisions and termination clause together define what the business actually is, and a hybrid path - sell for an operator now, credential and take over service later - is only real if the agreement's non-solicit and account-ownership terms permit it.

included: the two model shapes and their consequences for cost, liability, quality control and account ownership
the agreement clauses that must be read before any selling starts
hybrid and staged paths and what makes them viable
which party the customer contracts with and who is named on the paperwork
excluded: the licensing and certification requirement classes themselves and how an operator qualifies for them
drafting or legally interpreting the partnering agreement, which is counsel's work
retention economics and book valuation once the account base exists

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the operator agreement, its compensation exhibit, its territory grant or the seller's own credential status changes

pros.claim: Naming the model first fixes who owns the account, which is the single largest determinant of what this business is eventually worth
pros.example: reading the account-ownership clause of an operator agreement before canvassing a subdivision rather than discovering after eighty sales that every account belongs to the operator and follows it on termination

cons.claim: The comparison rests on variables the seller cannot observe in advance - service quality delivered by someone else, cancellation exposure, and how secure the territory grant really is
cons.example: choosing the commission model for its low capital requirement and then absorbing chargebacks caused by an operator who misses first-service appointments in peak season

failure_modes: selling for months without having read the account-ownership, territory or termination clauses
assuming a handshake referral arrangement conveys continuing residual income
drifting into performing application work the seller is not credentialed for because the partner operator is short-staffed
acceptance_tests: the chosen model is written down with a clause reference for each of: who applies pesticide, who owns the account, what territory is granted and how exclusively, how compensation is computed and reversed, and what happens on termination
revisit_triggers: the operator amends the agreement, the compensation exhibit or the territory grant
the seller obtains, or decides to pursue, operator credentials of their own
a second operator partnership is added or an existing one is terminated

nodes.definition: Build the map of where money actually arrives in this business and, for every line, record the mechanism that produces the number instead of the number itself. The lines are the initial or set-up service fee that covers the heavier first visit, the recurring service fee charged per visit or per month across an agreed frequency, the new-account commission or bounty in the sell-for-operator model, any continuing share of recurring revenue while the account persists, and separately priced additional work. For each line, write down the basis it is computed on - per account, per initial service, a percentage of collected revenue, a percentage of contract value - the timing at which it becomes payable, the drivers that move it up or down such as service frequency, property size, pest class, distance band and seasonal promotion, and above all the document that proves it: the operator's current price sheet and compensation exhibit, or in the own-operation model the seller's own published price list. The discipline that makes the map useful is that no figure enters it from memory, from a recruiter's pitch or from a competitor's claim; each is either read from a document for this specific deal or carried as a qualitative band with the verification step named beside it.

included: the inventory of revenue lines and the basis, timing and drivers of each
the document that proves each line and the per-deal verification step
distance, frequency and property characteristics as price drivers
how promotional pricing on the initial service changes the shape of first-year revenue
excluded: quoting any specific price, fee, rate or percentage as a fact
billing, term and renewal mechanics of the service agreement itself
the operator's internal cost base and how it sets its own margins

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a price sheet, compensation exhibit or promotional structure is published or revised

pros.claim: A mechanism map survives price changes, because it records how a number is produced rather than what it was on the day it was learned
pros.example: an operator re-tiers its initial-service pricing by property size and the map still answers what a given property will produce, since size was already recorded as the driver

cons.claim: Mechanism-level answers frustrate people who want a single figure, and the seller must resist supplying one to keep a conversation moving
cons.example: a prospective partner asking what a route is worth and receiving a list of drivers and a verification path instead of a number

failure_modes: repeating a commission or price figure heard in a recruiting conversation as though it were contractual
forgetting that a promotional initial-service price shifts revenue into later visits and mis-reading first-year economics
mixing gross contract value and collected cash in the same line so nothing reconciles
acceptance_tests: every revenue line carries a basis, a timing, at least one named driver and the specific document or clause a reader can check it against
revisit_triggers: the operator publishes a new price sheet or compensation exhibit
a promotion changes the initial-service or first-period pricing
a new service frequency or property class is offered for sale

nodes.definition: Hold the central fact of pest-control economics steadily in view: the recurring price a customer pays is roughly the same whether they are the fourth stop on one street or a lone account across the county, but the cost of serving them is not, because a technician's day is a fixed quantity of minutes and every mile between stops is time nobody pays for. Route density - how many serviceable accounts sit inside a radius small enough to work in a single route-day - is therefore the mechanism that turns an identical contract into a profitable account or a losing one. Density compounds in several directions at once: it shortens travel per stop, so more stops fit in a day; it makes the free re-service under the guarantee a five-minute detour instead of a half-day round trip; it makes appointment windows tight and reliable, which is itself a retention driver; it lowers the cost of the next sale, because the truck is already visible on the street; and it makes the book operable by someone other than its founder. The practical form of the principle is that the unit of sale here is not a customer but a customer in a place, and every prospective sale is judged by what it does to the route as well as by the revenue it adds.

included: density as the cost mechanism behind an identical contract
the compounding effects on re-service cost, window reliability, capacity and the cost of the next sale
the customer-in-a-place unit of sale
excluded: stop-sequence optimisation within a single day, which is a routing tool question
valuing the assembled book as a saleable asset
what the technician does once on site

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured travel minutes per stop diverge from the assumption the book was built on

pros.claim: Density reframes growth from counting accounts to clustering them, which changes every downstream decision from targeting to pacing
pros.example: declining a scattered set of five accounts spread across a county in favour of five neighbours on one cul-de-sac at the same recurring price

cons.claim: Applied rigidly the principle blocks all expansion, since the first account in any new area is by definition density-dilutive
cons.example: refusing an anchor account for a subdivision the plan intends to open next season because it currently sits alone

failure_modes: measuring growth in account count while average travel per stop quietly doubles
treating materials cost as the main variable cost when travel minutes dominate it
letting the principle harden into a rule that forbids opening any new geography
acceptance_tests: the operator can state, for a proposed sale, both the revenue it adds and its expected effect on travel minutes per stop in its zone
revisit_triggers: a zone's average travel per stop moves materially in either direction
the service frequency or the mix of property types in the book changes
a routing or scheduling change alters how stops are grouped

nodes.definition: Make drive time an explicit, measured line in the cost of an account instead of an invisible drain on the day. The mechanism is a decomposition: the total time an account consumes per visit equals the on-site service minutes, which are relatively stable for a routine treatment of a given property type, plus the travel minutes from the previous stop, plus the dead time the stop creates through gate access, parking, waiting for an occupant or re-locating equipment. Measure the travel component from real route evidence - timestamps between stops, odometer readings, the technician's own log - rather than from map estimates generated at a quiet hour, because the only number that matters is the drive at the time the route actually runs, on school-run mornings and in seasonal traffic. Convert those minutes into cost by applying the loaded cost of a technician minute and the vehicle cost per mile, both of which the operator can supply, and then attribute the result to the account whose position created it. The insight the mechanism reliably delivers is that a scattered account can consume two or three times the minutes of a clustered one while paying the same recurring fee, and that this difference usually dwarfs the entire materials cost of the visit, which is why cheap-chemistry reasoning misleads new entrants so consistently.

included: the per-stop time decomposition into service, travel and dead time
measuring travel from real route data at the hour routes run
loaded cost per minute and vehicle cost per mile as supplied mechanisms
attributing created travel to the account that created it
excluded: stating any specific wage, cost per mile or minute figure
vehicle purchase, leasing and fleet decisions
the treatment method performed during the on-site minutes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new route timestamp or odometer data changes measured travel minutes per stop

pros.claim: Once travel is measured per stop, arguments about which accounts are worth keeping become arithmetic instead of opinion
pros.example: a rural account whose logged stop-to-stop time is several times the zone median showing up as the reason a route-day cannot absorb another sale

cons.claim: Honest measurement takes weeks of route data and can be resisted by technicians who read logging as surveillance
cons.example: timestamp logging introduced mid-season being filled in retrospectively and producing a smoothed, useless picture

failure_modes: using off-peak map estimates as though they were route reality
averaging travel across the whole territory so dense and scattered zones look identical
ignoring access dead time at gated properties, which behaves exactly like travel
acceptance_tests: each active zone has stop-to-stop travel measured from real route records within the current season, and the per-stop decomposition names service, travel and dead-time minutes separately
revisit_triggers: a road, construction or traffic-pattern change alters travel inside a zone
route sequencing or day assignment changes
a new property class with different on-site time enters the book

nodes.definition: Draw the actual geography this business will sell inside, and split it into named zones that map onto service days. This is a map exercise with hard edges rather than an aspiration: an outer boundary beyond which accounts are declined, parked or referred; internal zone polygons sized so that a full route-day fits comfortably inside one; boundaries that follow real barriers such as highways, rivers, canals, rail lines, city limits and gated communities rather than tidy circles drawn around an office; a service-day assignment per zone; and an explicit list of edge accounts sitting near a seam that may be reassigned between zones as the book grows. Zone edges should follow drive-time contours rather than distance, because ten miles along an arterial can be nearer in minutes than three miles across a congested grid at the wrong hour. The territory map doubles as the compliance map, since solicitation permits, do-not-knock registries and private community rules attach to the municipalities and communities the polygon crosses, and because the servicing operator's own authority to work may itself stop at a county or state line - a fact to verify before a zone is drawn across one.

included: outer boundary, zone polygons on drive-time contours and service-day assignment
barrier-aware boundaries and the edge-account list
overlay of municipal and community boundaries that carry sales rules
the note that the servicing operator's authority may end at a jurisdiction line
excluded: asserting what any named jurisdiction currently requires
sequencing stops inside a day
the depth of licensing-footprint verification for the operator

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a zone saturates, a barrier or development changes travel, or the operator's authorised area moves

pros.claim: A drawn boundary converts every distance decision from a negotiation into a lookup, and makes an honest no possible at the door
pros.example: telling a caller two towns away that service starts there when the zone opens, and adding them to a named waitlist instead of improvising

cons.claim: Any boundary cuts through real demand and will be tested constantly by good prospects who sit just outside it
cons.example: a large referral source whose portfolio straddles the seam between an open zone and one not yet seeded

failure_modes: drawing circles around an office instead of drive-time contours
letting the map drift into an unbounded region as exceptions accumulate
crossing a municipal or jurisdictional line without re-checking the sales and licensing overlay
acceptance_tests: the map shows an outer boundary, named zones with a service-day assignment, a marked edge-account list, and the municipal and community boundaries each zone crosses
revisit_triggers: a zone's accounts outgrow a single route-day
a new development, road or barrier changes travel inside the territory
the servicing operator's authorised working area changes

nodes.definition: Model what one technician-day can genuinely hold, because that is the resource each sale spends. Build it from components rather than from a remembered number: working minutes in the day, minus start-up, re-stock, paperwork and end-of-day time, divided by the average minutes per stop for the property type in that zone - service plus travel plus access dead time - then adjusted downward for the share of stops needing interior access and a booked window, for the re-services and callbacks that must fit into the same day, and for weather, no-access and reschedule losses that are certain to occur across a season. Convert stops per day into accounts supported: at a given service frequency each account claims a slot several times a year, so the book a route can carry is stops per day times service days per cycle divided by visits per account per cycle. Express the result as a band with its assumptions written beside it rather than a single false-precision figure, and re-derive it per zone, because a dense subdivision of similar homes and a rural spread of long driveways produce very different capacities from the same technician on the same day.

included: the component build of a route-day and its loss adjustments
conversion from stops per day to accounts supported at a service frequency
per-zone re-derivation and band presentation with assumptions
excluded: scheduling software configuration
hiring, training and credentialing lead time for adding a technician
choosing the service frequency as a contract term

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: completed stops per day, callback volume or property mix diverge from the modelled band

pros.claim: A component model tells you not just how full the route is but which component to attack when it is full
pros.example: seeing that interior-access windows rather than travel are consuming the capacity of a zone of older homes, and re-sequencing the day around them

cons.claim: The model is only as good as its loss assumptions, and seasonal losses are exactly what an inexperienced operator underestimates
cons.example: a capacity band built without a weather allowance collapsing during a wet fortnight when half the exterior services are pushed

failure_modes: quoting a single stops-per-day number with no assumptions attached
forgetting that callbacks and re-services consume slots the model already sold
applying one zone's capacity to a zone with different property types
acceptance_tests: each active zone has a stops-per-day band with its working-minute, per-stop and loss assumptions listed, and a derived accounts-supported figure at the service frequency actually sold
revisit_triggers: measured stops completed per day diverge from the modelled band
the mix of property types or the share of interior-access services changes
a technician is added, removed or reassigned between zones

nodes.definition: Read where genuine, recurring pest pressure comes from, so that targeting rests on observable conditions rather than on guesswork or on whichever neighbourhood is closest to home. Pressure is produced by habitat and structure interacting at a scale of streets rather than cities: standing water in irrigation canals, drainage ditches, retention ponds and neglected pools; greenbelts, wooded edges, agricultural margins and recently cleared land that push displaced populations toward structures; dense foundation planting, heavy mulch beds, wood piles and wood-to-soil contact; construction age and method, which changes the entry points a building offers and its slab or crawlspace exposure; the density of adjacent units, which lets pressure travel between homes regardless of who treats; and concentrated food sources such as dumpsters, pet food, fruit trees and poorly managed bins. Read it in the field by walking a neighbourhood and looking at eaves, weep holes, mulch lines, grade against siding and rubbish staging, and by listening to people who are inside structures all day. The output is a pressure read per micro-geography, and it matters twice over: it marks where selling is honest and easy because the need is real, and it marks where the recurring service will visibly work, which is what makes the account survive its first year.

included: habitat, structural and land-use drivers of recurring pressure at neighbourhood scale
the field-walk method for reading a micro-geography
the link between genuine pressure, honest selling and account survival
excluded: identifying species or diagnosing an infestation at a specific property
recommending any treatment or product
asserting local pest biology or emergence timing as established fact rather than as a pattern to verify locally

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: field observation or service records from a zone contradict the recorded pressure drivers

pros.claim: Targeting on visible conditions produces accounts that experience the service working, which is the cheapest retention there is
pros.example: prioritising a subdivision backing onto a canal and greenbelt over an identically priced inland tract with no adjacent habitat

cons.claim: A field read is qualitative and can be over-generalised from one street to a whole subdivision
cons.example: assuming an entire development shares the drainage problem observed on its lowest two streets

failure_modes: confusing a one-off seasonal event with sustained recurring pressure
reading pressure from a competitor's advertising volume instead of from conditions
sliding from conditions language into diagnostic claims the seller is not competent to make
acceptance_tests: each target micro-geography carries at least two named observed drivers and the date the field read was made
revisit_triggers: land use changes nearby, such as clearing, construction or a new water feature
a season passes and the observed pressure pattern differs from the read
service records from the zone contradict the pressure assumption

nodes.definition: Turn the pressure read into a ranked, working list of neighbourhoods, using criteria that predict both a fair close and a route that pays. The stack of criteria is: observed pest pressure; homogeneity of the housing stock, because similar homes consume similar service minutes and make capacity predictable; owner-occupancy share, since owners can authorise service on their property and tenants frequently cannot; doors per street-mile, which is raw density available to be bought; visible upkeep of properties as an honest proxy for willingness to buy a recurring service; access rules, which sort neighbourhoods into open, gated, HOA-governed and posted-no-soliciting classes long before a canvass plan exists; competitor saturation, readable from service stickers, yard signs and truck sightings; and distance from an existing cluster or a zone the plan already intends to open. The output is a ranked list with a written reason per neighbourhood, worked in order, rather than a scatter of effort following wherever the week's leads happened to land. One rule sits above the criteria: targeting is done on pest, property and access facts, never on the race, national origin, religion, familial status or other protected characteristics of who lives there, and never on a demographic proxy standing in for them.

included: the ranking criteria and the rationale for each
the ranked target list as a working artifact with reasons
access-class and competitor-saturation reads
excluded: targeting or avoiding neighbourhoods on protected characteristics or proxies for them
asserting income or demographic figures for an area
the doorstep conversation itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: conversion, cancellation or access data from a worked neighbourhood contradicts its ranking reason

pros.claim: A written ranking makes canvass effort cumulative instead of scattered, and the reasons can be audited when a neighbourhood underperforms
pros.example: discovering that the two lowest-converting targets were both ranked mainly on doors per mile with no pressure driver recorded

cons.claim: Criteria that look neutral can become proxies for protected characteristics if applied carelessly, which is both unlawful in many places and a poor predictor of who buys
cons.example: using an area's perceived affluence rather than observed property upkeep and pest pressure as the ranking driver

failure_modes: ranking on distance from home rather than on pressure and access
ignoring the owner-occupancy read and generating contracts nobody at the door can authorise
letting a demographic proxy substitute for a property-and-pressure criterion
acceptance_tests: every neighbourhood on the list carries a written reason built only from pest, property, access and route facts, and the list is worked in rank order
revisit_triggers: conversion or cancellation data from a worked neighbourhood contradicts its rank
a competitor saturates or exits a target area
an access rule changes, such as a new gated entry or HOA policy

nodes.definition: Open new geography deliberately: place an anchor first, then fill around it, rather than accepting scattered accounts and hoping they eventually knit themselves into a route. An anchor is an account or cluster substantial enough to justify the drive on its own - a property manager's portfolio in one complex, a group referred through an HOA introduction, a commercial account on a service frequency, or a first residential sale on the highest-pressure street of the target subdivision. Once the anchor exists, selling effort concentrates inside the smallest radius that can be walked in a working day, using neighbour referrals, repeat passes at different hours to catch households who are out, and the plain visibility of a service truck parked on the street. Progress is measured as penetration - the share of doors in the target block or subdivision that are live accounts - and the zone is not treated as open until penetration supports a stop count worth the drive. The seeding period is knowingly unprofitable, so the discipline is to keep it short, bounded and confined to one zone at a time; seeding five zones simultaneously produces five thin, unprofitable routes and a business that feels busy while losing money on every mile.

included: anchor selection and what qualifies as one
concentric fill technique and repeat-pass timing
penetration as the progress measure and the open-zone threshold
one-zone-at-a-time discipline with a bounded seeding period
excluded: the service agreement terms offered to a portfolio client
the service schedule build once accounts exist
paying for introductions in ways that are not disclosed to the end customer

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: penetration in a seeding zone crosses or stalls at the open-zone threshold, or an anchor is lost

pros.claim: Anchoring converts the unavoidable cost of opening geography into a bounded, budgeted investment with a visible exit test
pros.example: seeding on a managed complex and stopping the subsidy once penetration on the surrounding blocks supports a full route-day

cons.claim: Anchors concentrate risk: one portfolio decision-maker leaving can strip the reason the zone was ever driven to
cons.example: a property manager changing vendors and taking the only cluster in a half-opened zone with them

failure_modes: seeding several zones at once and being unprofitably thin in all of them
letting the seeding period run indefinitely because sales are still arriving
measuring fill in accounts sold rather than in penetration of the target blocks
acceptance_tests: each open or opening zone names its anchor, its fill radius, its current penetration and the penetration level at which seeding ends
revisit_triggers: an anchor account or portfolio is lost
penetration stalls below the open-zone threshold for a full season
a higher-ranked neighbourhood becomes available inside the same drive

nodes.definition: Apply a standing test to every prospective account that sits outside an existing cluster, so distance decisions are made by rule rather than by mood in the moment of an easy sale. The test runs in order. Does this account anchor a zone the plan already intends to open? Does it arrive with neighbours, a portfolio or an introduction that creates a cluster immediately rather than eventually? Can it be absorbed by scheduling - grouped onto a single day with other outliers, or attached to a route that already passes it on the way to somewhere else? Can a distance-aware price band be applied honestly, disclosed plainly to the customer, and still leave the account contributing? And if none of those hold, is the honest answer to park it on a named waitlist until the zone opens, or to refer it to another operator who already serves that area? Whichever branch is taken, the decision and its reason are recorded against the lead. The value of the test is not that distant accounts are always refused - it is that they are never accepted by accident, and that the seller can explain to a homeowner without embarrassment why service is not available there yet.

included: the ordered accept-cluster-absorb-price-park-refer test
waitlist and referral-out as legitimate recorded outcomes
the recorded decision and reason against each out-of-cluster lead
excluded: quoting a distance surcharge as a figure
declining service on any basis other than route, capacity and authority facts
renegotiating the price of an account already in force

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: scorecard evidence on outlier accounts, or the opening of a parked lead's zone, changes the standing decision

pros.claim: A written test removes the argument from every distance decision and makes refusals consistent and explainable
pros.example: two similar out-of-zone leads in the same week receiving the same parked-with-reason outcome instead of one being taken because the day had gone badly

cons.claim: Any rule applied to a live prospect costs revenue today for density tomorrow, and the cost is felt immediately while the benefit is diffuse
cons.example: parking a willing high-value prospect who then buys from a competitor and never returns when the zone opens

failure_modes: taking the account anyway and letting the route absorb an invisible loss
applying a distance price without disclosing plainly why it differs
parking a lead with no waitlist, no reason recorded and no follow-up
acceptance_tests: every out-of-cluster lead carries one of the five recorded outcomes with its reason, and parked leads sit on a named waitlist tied to a zone
revisit_triggers: a parked lead's zone opens or is dropped from the plan
the density scorecard shows outlier accounts degrading a zone's travel per stop
a distance price band is introduced or withdrawn

nodes.definition: Before a single door is knocked or a neighbourhood campaign is planned, clear the classes of rule that govern selling at a consumer's home, and clear them per municipality, because they can differ from one side of a boundary road to the other. The classes to check are: solicitor, peddler or transient-merchant permit and registration requirements, which often carry an application, a fee, a background check and a badge that must be worn and shown; permitted hours and days for solicitation; municipal do-not-knock registries where they exist and the legal weight given locally to posted no-soliciting signage; private restrictions imposed by gated communities, homeowner associations and property managers, which bind regardless of what municipal law allows; the home-solicitation cooling-off or right-to-cancel class of consumer protection that commonly attaches to sales made at a consumer's residence, including the written notice that must be given and the form it must take; registration classes that some jurisdictions attach specifically to people who sell pest control services even when they never apply a product; and the rules governing telephone, text and email follow-up to someone met at a door. Nothing here is asserted as a current specific rule. The deliverable is a per-municipality checklist naming the class, the authority to ask, the date checked and the answer obtained, refreshed on a stated cadence, because these rules change and enforcement is intensely local.

included: the obligation classes governing home solicitation and follow-up contact
the dated per-municipality checklist with the authority consulted
badge and permit carrying, honoring registries and posted signage, private community rules
the cooling-off and written-notice class attached to home sales
excluded: asserting any named jurisdiction's current rule, fee, hour or notice wording
pesticide operator and applicator licensing classes, which are the delivery knowledge base's territory
legal advice, which comes from counsel and the regulator

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a municipal ordinance, do-not-knock registry, community rule or consumer-cancellation requirement is enacted or amended in a worked area

pros.claim: Clearing the screen per municipality before planning turns compliance into a one-time cost per area instead of an enforcement event mid-campaign
pros.example: learning that a target city requires a registered badge and restricts evening hours before a summer canvass schedule is built around evenings

cons.claim: The screen is slow, must be repeated per municipality and per season, and its answers expire
cons.example: a checklist cleared in spring that no longer reflects an ordinance amended before the autumn rodent push

failure_modes: assuming one city's permit rules apply across a metropolitan area
treating a posted no-soliciting sign as advisory
omitting the written cancellation notice class from the paperwork given at the door
following up by phone or text in ways the contact rules do not permit
acceptance_tests: every municipality in the canvass plan has a dated checklist entry naming the permit, hours, registry, signage, private-community and cancellation-notice classes, the authority consulted and the verify-locally note
no canvass route is walked in a municipality whose checklist entry is missing or older than the stated refresh cadence
revisit_triggers: an ordinance, registry or enforcement practice changes in a worked municipality
the canvass plan extends into a municipality not yet screened
a complaint, citation or refusal of entry occurs in the field

nodes.definition: Bind every claim made to a prospect to something observed and shown, and keep three tiers rigidly separate. The first tier is conducive conditions - mulch banked against siding, wood-to-soil contact, standing water, dense harborage in foundation planting, gaps at weep holes and door sweeps, an unscreened crawl vent - which anyone can see, which the homeowner can be walked to, and which honestly support a prevention conversation. The second tier is observed activity: a trail, webbing, frass, droppings, gnaw marks, a nest, damage that is actually present, photographed with its location and date recorded. The third tier is diagnosis - naming an infestation, its extent, or the presence of wood-destroying organisms - which is a licensed inspection judgement, is referred out rather than asserted, and never becomes a closing argument in a doorstep conversation. The discipline is procedural, not merely attitudinal: photograph and note what was shown, describe it in plain language without species or extent claims that exceed the seller's competence, record it on the account so the technician arrives seeing the same thing, and when a prospect asks a question that requires a licensed opinion, say so plainly and arrange the inspection. Manufactured urgency is prohibited not only because it is dishonest but because it produces accounts that cancel at the first invoice, chargebacks, complaints and the kind of local reputation that closes a whole territory permanently.

included: the three-tier separation of conditions, observed activity and diagnosis
photographing, locating and dating what is shown, and recording it on the account
referring licensed-opinion questions rather than answering them
the prohibition on invented findings, fabricated neighbour stories and manufactured deadlines
excluded: performing the inspection or diagnosis itself
recommending a treatment, product or rate
the licensed operator's own reporting duties for regulated findings

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint, review or technician report contradicts what a sale record says was observed

pros.claim: Showing a real condition outperforms pressure as persuasion and produces accounts that survive their first invoice
pros.example: walking a homeowner to the mulch line banked over the siding and the gap under the garage door rather than describing an unseen infestation

cons.claim: Evidence-bound selling closes fewer doors per hour and loses head-to-head against a competitor willing to exaggerate
cons.example: a prospect signing with a canvasser who promised to eliminate a termite problem nobody has inspected for

failure_modes: asserting an infestation or wood-destroying-organism finding without a licensed inspection
using a neighbour's real pest problem as a closing device and breaching that neighbour's privacy
letting conditions language slide into extent and species claims
recording no evidence, leaving the technician to arrive at a property with a different story
acceptance_tests: every sale record carries at least one dated, located observation or photograph of what was actually shown to the prospect
no sale record or script contains a diagnostic claim, a fabricated neighbour reference or a manufactured deadline
revisit_triggers: a complaint or review alleges a misrepresented finding
a technician reports that what was recorded at the sale is not present at the property
scripts or leave-behind material are revised

nodes.definition: Recognise at the door the situations in which an ordinary sales process is not adequate, and slow down or stop. Two families of concern arise. The first is capacity and comprehension: an occupant who appears confused or cannot recall what was just discussed, who does not read or speak the language of the paperwork, who is visibly distressed or unwell, who is plainly isolated and eager for company, or who defers repeatedly to an absent family member. The correct response is to leave written information and identification, offer to return when a family member, carer or interpreter can be present, and decline to take a signature that day even when it is offered. The second family is household sensitivity that changes what may honestly be promised: pregnancy, asthma and respiratory illness, chemical sensitivity, infants and young children, indoor and outdoor pets, aquariums and ponds, backyard hives and pollinator plantings, edible gardens and small livestock. The seller's duty is not to adjudicate these - that is licensed, label-governed judgement belonging to the operator - but to ask, record them verbatim, refuse to promise around them, and route them to the licensed operator before any service is committed. The working test is simple and strict: a sale that would embarrass you if the household's family heard the recording is a sale to decline.

included: stop-the-sale triggers for doubtful capacity or comprehension
the return-with-a-family-member-or-interpreter practice and written leave-behind
the sensitivity classes to elicit, record verbatim and escalate
the rule that the seller never promises around a health, pet or pollinator concern
excluded: deciding whether a product or method is appropriate given a stated sensitivity, which is the licensed operator's judgement
medical advice of any kind
the treatment plan or its label-driven constraints

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint, family contact or operator policy change reveals a gap in how consent and sensitivity are handled at the door

pros.claim: Declining a doubtful-consent sale removes the single most damaging category of complaint this industry generates and protects the territory's reputation
pros.example: leaving literature and a callback offer with an elderly resident who could not recall the conversation, rather than taking the signature offered

cons.claim: The judgement is made in seconds by a salesperson with an incentive to close, and honest sellers will sometimes decline sales that would have been fine
cons.example: walking away from a competent older homeowner who simply wanted time to think and then bought elsewhere

failure_modes: taking a signature from someone who cannot recall the conversation minutes later
using a household member or child to translate a contract conversation
reassuring a prospect about safety around pets, hives or a garden instead of routing the question to the licensed operator
recording a stated sensitivity nowhere, so the technician arrives without knowing
acceptance_tests: any sale where a capacity or comprehension concern arose shows either a decline, or a documented return visit with a family member or interpreter present
every stated health, pet, pollinator or garden sensitivity appears verbatim on the account record and is flagged to the licensed operator before the first service
revisit_triggers: a family member, carer or advocate contacts the business about a sale
a complaint alleges pressure on a vulnerable occupant
the operator changes how sensitivity flags are handled before service

nodes.definition: Establish, before a signature exists, that the person in front of you can actually bind this property to a recurring service and consent to treatment on it. The commonest failure is the tenant who cheerfully signs a service the landlord already buys, forbids, or is contractually responsible for; the same shape recurs with a household member without authority, a property manager whose mandate covers interior work but not exterior or structural services, an association that governs common areas but not the units inside them, a commercial tenant whose lease assigns pest control to the landlord, and a property mid-sale, in probate or under a rental-management agreement nobody at the door has read. The method is unglamorous: ask plainly whether they own or rent, who pays for services at the property, and whether an existing contract or management agreement already covers pest control, then record the answer on the lead. Where authority is unclear, obtain it in writing from the party who holds it before service is scheduled rather than proceeding on a confident verbal assurance, because an account taken from someone without authority cancels early, generally inside the clawback window, and it can leave a household paying twice for the same service.

included: the tenant, household member, property manager, association, commercial-lease and transaction cases
the plain questions asked and recorded at the door
written confirmation from the authority holder before scheduling
excluded: interpreting a lease or management agreement as legal advice
the service agreement's own signature and term provisions
resolving a dispute between a landlord and a tenant

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cancellations or duplicate-coverage complaints trace back to who signed at the door

pros.claim: A thirty-second authority check removes a whole class of early cancellation and the chargeback that rides with it
pros.example: asking who pays for services at the property and discovering the landlord's management company already holds a pest-control contract

cons.claim: The questions can feel intrusive at a doorstep and occasionally cost a sale that would have stood
cons.example: a long-term tenant with genuine authority under an unusual lease being routed to the landlord and losing interest

failure_modes: accepting a confident verbal claim of ownership without recording it
selling a whole complex through an on-site person whose mandate does not extend to units
signing an owner-required exterior or structural service through a tenant
acceptance_tests: every sale record states owner or tenant status, who pays for services at the property, and whether an existing contract covers it
no service is scheduled where authority was unclear without written confirmation from the party holding it
revisit_triggers: a property changes hands, tenants or management company
a cancellation cites lack of authority or duplicate coverage
a portfolio client changes the scope of its mandate

nodes.definition: Run the doorstep conversation so that it would survive being replayed to the homeowner's adult child, to a regulator, and on a review site. Its shape is fixed. Identify yourself by name, name the licensed operator who will perform the service and state your relationship to it, and give the purpose of the visit in the first sentence rather than the fourth. Ask permission to continue, and stop cleanly at the first clear no without a second attempt. Walk only where you are invited, and show what you actually observe rather than what usually exists in houses like this one. Explain the recurring service at the level a person can repeat afterwards: what it covers and does not, how often the technician comes, what happens between visits under the guarantee, how billing works and how the agreement ends. Leave written material and your identification whether or not there is a sale, including the cancellation notice class the jurisdiction requires. Never deploy urgency, a fabricated neighbour story, a manufactured deadline, a discount that expires when you walk away, or a fear claim. The craft in this is not softness: showing real conditions and plain mechanics converts better among people who will still be customers in a year, and this business is built entirely out of accounts that survive.

included: the identify, disclose, ask-permission, show, explain, leave-written sequence
stopping at the first no and the invited-walk rule
plain-language explanation of coverage, frequency, guarantee, billing and ending
the prohibition on urgency, fear and fabricated social proof
excluded: the drafting and clause-level terms of the service agreement
treatment claims requiring licensed judgement
any script built on scarcity, fear or fabricated neighbour evidence

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cancellation reasons, complaints or mystery-shop reviews reveal what the doorstep conversation is actually saying

pros.claim: A disclosure-first conversation produces customers who can explain what they bought, which is the strongest predictor of surviving the first invoice
pros.example: a customer telling the technician on the first visit exactly which areas are covered and what the re-service arrangement is

cons.claim: Full disclosure lengthens every conversation and lowers doors-per-hour, which looks like weakness on a raw activity dashboard
cons.example: a canvasser who explains cancellation mechanics unprompted closing fewer doors per shift than one who does not

failure_modes: leading with a hook and disclosing the sales purpose only after interest is established
continuing after a clear refusal or returning the same day
explaining price while leaving frequency, guarantee and ending mechanics vague
leaving no written material and no identification behind
acceptance_tests: a randomly sampled recent customer can state the service frequency, what is covered, the re-service arrangement and how to end the agreement
every contacted household received written material and seller identification, and no record shows contact continuing after a refusal
revisit_triggers: complaint volume or early-cancellation reasons point at what was said at the door
the operator changes the service description or guarantee wording
a regulatory checklist entry changes what must be disclosed or left behind

nodes.definition: Compute, as a mechanism rather than a headline, what a single account contributes once the route has been charged for serving it. Begin with recurring revenue over a year - fee per visit multiplied by visits per year at the agreed frequency, plus the initial service fee in the first year. Subtract materials consumed per visit; the loaded cost of the on-site minutes; the allocated travel minutes the account's position adds to its route, taken from measured stop-to-stop data rather than from an average; the expected cost of free re-services under the guarantee, which is a frequency multiplied by a cost that itself depends on distance; and the billing, insurance and administrative load per account. Against the resulting annual contribution, set the acquisition cost - commission paid, canvass hours consumed, marketing spend attributable to the account - and express payback as a number of service visits rather than months, because visits are what the route actually delivers. Two conclusions fall out with great regularity: the identical contract is strongly profitable inside a cluster and negative outside it, and a modestly priced account that never cancels outperforms a richly priced one that leaves in its first year. Every element stays a named driver with a verification path; no element is published as a figure.

included: the contribution build from recurring revenue through materials, on-site minutes, allocated travel, guarantee re-service and admin load
acquisition cost and payback expressed in service visits
the cluster-versus-outlier comparison for an identical contract
excluded: publishing any specific cost, price, margin or payback figure
lifetime-value modelling and retention curves of the in-force book
valuing the book for sale or financing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured travel, material, labour, guarantee or acquisition costs move enough to change the sign of an account class

pros.claim: Charging travel to the account that creates it turns density from a slogan into a line item that decides individual sales
pros.example: the same quarterly contract showing positive contribution on a cul-de-sac and negative contribution for an isolated account well outside the cluster once its travel share is applied

cons.claim: Allocating shared route time to a single account is inherently approximate and can be gamed by choosing a convenient allocation basis
cons.example: attributing travel evenly across a day's stops so an isolated account hides behind its neighbours' short hops

failure_modes: omitting the guarantee re-service cost, which is precisely the cost distance inflates
measuring payback in months while the route delivers value in visits
treating the first-year promotional price as the account's steady state
acceptance_tests: the contribution model for a zone names every subtraction with its driver and its source, and payback is expressed in service visits
at least one clustered and one outlier account are computed side by side so the density effect is visible
revisit_triggers: measured travel per stop, material cost or the loaded technician rate changes
the guarantee or re-service practice changes
commission or acquisition cost per account changes

nodes.definition: Read the compensation exhibit as a machine that shapes selling behaviour, and write down its parts explicitly. The basis: a flat amount per new account, a percentage of the initial service fee, a share of collected recurring revenue, a share of contract value, or a combination that changes with volume. The vesting event: payable on signature, on completion of the first service, on collection of the first payment, or staged across several. The clawback or chargeback condition: cancellation within a stated window, non-payment, or a sale later found unauthorised or misrepresented - together with how the reversal is taken, whether from future commissions, from a held reserve, or pursued as a debt. Any quality adjustment tied to cancellation rate, complaint volume or first-service success. And the treatment of continuing residual payments while an account persists, including what happens to them if the agreement terminates. Naming these matters because the structure determines which accounts are worth selling: front-loaded pay with a reversal window rewards accounts that survive the window, residual pay rewards accounts that survive for years, and pay on signature with no reversal at all rewards volume regardless of truth - a structure a careful seller should read as a warning about the operator rather than as an opportunity. Every element is read from the actual exhibit; none is assumed, and none is quoted here as a figure.

included: basis, vesting event, clawback condition and recovery method, quality adjustments, residual treatment on termination
the behavioural consequence of each structure for which accounts are worth selling
reading each element from the actual compensation exhibit
excluded: stating any commission rate, bounty amount, reserve percentage or window length as a fact
worker-classification, tax or employment-law advice about how a seller is engaged
the operator's internal margin on the account

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the compensation exhibit is amended, or a pay statement shows a reversal the written mechanism does not explain

pros.claim: Knowing the vesting and reversal terms converts commission from a hope into a forecastable, defendable number tied to account survival
pros.example: recognising that pay vesting on collected first payment makes access failures at first service a direct pay problem, not just a scheduling one

cons.claim: The structure is set by the operator and is largely non-negotiable for a small seller, so the knowledge often only tells you which accounts to avoid
cons.example: learning that the reversal window is long and that cancellations in it are recovered from future pay, with no ability to change the term

failure_modes: selling hard into a structure that pays on signature and ignoring whether accounts survive
budgeting on gross commission and being surprised by reversals taken from later pay
assuming residual payments continue after the agreement ends
acceptance_tests: the compensation mechanism is written down with basis, vesting event, reversal condition, recovery method and residual treatment, each pointing at a clause of the actual exhibit
a reversal that has occurred can be reconciled line by line against that written mechanism
revisit_triggers: the operator revises the compensation exhibit or its reversal window
an unexplained or disputed reversal appears in a pay statement
a new product, frequency or territory carries different compensation

nodes.definition: Work customer referrals as the channel native to route density, because a referral from a customer is almost always geographically adjacent to that customer - the neighbour across the fence, the sister two streets over, the colleague in the same subdivision - which means each one lands inside or beside an existing cluster and costs the least of any account to acquire. Build it deliberately rather than hoping for it. Ask at the moment value is visible, after a service the customer can see worked, not at the point of sale when nothing has been demonstrated. Make the ask specific and local - a street, a neighbour with the same problem the customer had - rather than a generic request to spread the word. Give the customer something concrete to hand over. Disclose any referral incentive to both sides, including on the new customer's paperwork, so a compensated recommendation is never presented as disinterested advice. Contact the referral as a warm introduction the referrer has agreed to, never as a lead handed to a canvasser who arrives cold and names the neighbour, which both burns the relationship and can disclose the referrer's own pest problem without permission. Because referral accounts carry near-zero acquisition cost and land inside the cluster, they change account contribution twice over.

included: timing the ask to demonstrated value
street-specific asks and a concrete handover artifact
incentive disclosure to both parties and on the new customer's paperwork
warm-introduction rule and the referring customer's privacy
excluded: the retention and service-quality practice that creates the referable result
quoting a referral incentive amount
using a neighbour's pest problem as a cold-call opener

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: referral volume per account, incentive terms or a referrer complaint changes how the channel is run

pros.claim: Referrals arrive pre-clustered and pre-trusted, improving both the route and the conversion rate at once
pros.example: three accounts on one street arriving from one satisfied customer after a visible ant problem stopped

cons.claim: Referral volume is a lagging, uncontrollable function of service quality delivered by someone else in the partner model
cons.example: a referral engine going silent for a season because the servicing operator missed appointments across the zone

failure_modes: asking for referrals at the sale, before anything has been demonstrated
paying an incentive without disclosing it to the referred customer
handing referral names to a cold canvass and naming the referrer at the door
revealing what service the referring household receives
acceptance_tests: every referral record shows the referrer's agreement to the introduction and, where an incentive exists, its disclosure to both parties
no referral is contacted with details of the referrer's own service or pest history
revisit_triggers: referral volume per active account changes materially
an incentive is introduced, changed or withdrawn
a referrer objects to how their introduction was used

nodes.definition: Cultivate the referral sources that can deliver density through one relationship instead of one door at a time: property managers and landlords holding several units inside a single zone, association boards and community managers who can introduce a whole development, realtors and home inspectors who meet households at transaction moments, builders finishing new phases, and adjacent trades - lawn care, landscaping, cleaning, pool service, home watch - whose crews are on properties every week and see conditions before anyone else. Each type is worked differently: portfolios need one decision-maker, a written service standard and predictable scheduling; transaction sources need speed and a clean document they can hand a client; trade partners need reciprocity that is actually reciprocal rather than a one-way lead extraction. Two constraints run through all of them. Referral compensation must be disclosed to the end customer, and some professions and jurisdictions restrict or prohibit referral fees or require specific disclosure, so the arrangement class must be verified with counsel and the relevant regulator rather than copied from what a competitor appears to be doing. And a portfolio that arrives all at once is a capacity event as much as a sales win: signed in one afternoon, it consumes route slots for weeks and, if unpaced, produces late first services across every unit simultaneously.

included: portfolio, transaction, builder and trade source types and how each is worked
referral-compensation disclosure and the verification class for referral-fee restrictions
the capacity consequence of a portfolio landing at once
excluded: asserting whether a referral fee is permitted for a named profession or jurisdiction
the portfolio client's service agreement terms and renewal mechanics
an arrangement that would pay for a recommendation without disclosure to the customer

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a partner mandate, vendor policy or referral-compensation rule changes, or a portfolio's size inside a zone moves

pros.claim: One portfolio relationship can create a cluster that would take a season of canvassing to assemble door by door
pros.example: a managed complex inside a target zone becoming the anchor that makes the surrounding blocks worth walking

cons.claim: Concentration cuts both ways: a single decision-maker can remove a large share of a zone's density in one conversation
cons.example: a management company consolidating vendors and ending the arrangement that justified opening the zone

failure_modes: accepting a portfolio without pacing its onboarding against route capacity
paying or receiving referral compensation without disclosure to the end customer
assuming an on-site contact has authority over the units
treating a trade partnership as a one-way lead source until the partner disengages
acceptance_tests: each partner arrangement records who the customer contracts with, what compensation flows in either direction, and how it is disclosed to the end customer
each portfolio has an onboarding schedule that fits the receiving zone's route capacity
revisit_triggers: a partner's decision-maker, mandate or vendor policy changes
the verification of referral-fee permissibility becomes stale or a rule changes
a portfolio's units grow or shrink materially inside a zone

nodes.definition: Handle inbound demand - local search, map listings, review sites, yard signage, a truck parked visibly on a street, and plain word of mouth - in full knowledge that it arrives wherever it happens to arrive and is therefore density-blind by nature. The discipline is triage rather than refusal. An inbound lead inside an open zone is filled immediately and treated as the cheapest account available. A lead just outside a zone seam is put through the dilution test like any other outlier. A recurring cluster of inbound leads from one area is read as a demand signal that may justify seeding a zone there, since people who call are already sold on the need. An isolated distant lead is parked on a waitlist or referred out with an honest explanation of why service is not available yet. Because inbound leads convert far better than cold doors and cost far less to acquire, they are also the right accounts to spend as anchors when a new zone is being opened. Track where inbound demand comes from geographically and not merely how much of it there is: the map of who is calling is the cheapest market research this business will ever have access to, and it frequently contradicts the ranking assembled from field observation.

included: triage of inbound leads by position relative to open zones
reading geographic clusters of inbound demand as a seeding signal
using high-intent inbound accounts as anchors
mapping inbound origin as market research
excluded: advertising channel buying, budgeting and creative production
the review and reputation practice that generates inbound over time
promising a start date before a route slot exists

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the geographic distribution of inbound leads shifts enough to change seeding or ranking decisions

pros.claim: Inbound demand carries intent, so it converts at a fraction of the effort of a cold door and can be spent where it does the most for the route
pros.example: using two inbound calls from the same new development as the anchor pair for opening that zone

cons.claim: Inbound arrives on the customer's geography and schedule, which pulls a disciplined territory plan apart if every call is simply taken
cons.example: a month of scattered inbound accounts across four unopened areas leaving no zone with a workable stop count

failure_modes: taking every inbound call regardless of position because it feels free
recording lead volume without recording lead geography
promising a start date at the moment of the call before a slot exists
acceptance_tests: inbound leads are logged with their location and routed through the same accept, absorb, price, park or refer decision as any other outlier
the inbound origin map is reviewed against the neighbourhood ranking at a stated cadence
revisit_triggers: inbound volume from an unopened area crosses the level that would justify seeding
the inbound origin map contradicts the current target ranking
a new listing, sign or review source changes where inbound comes from

nodes.definition: Plan the year around the fact that both pest pressure and willingness to buy move in waves, and that the waves differ by pest class and by climate zone. In broad, qualitative classes: warm-season pressure from ants, spiders, wasps and mosquitoes builds through spring and peaks in summer heat; cooling weather pushes rodents toward the warmth of structures in autumn; wood-destroying-organism activity has its own visible emergence periods that generate inspection demand; and some indoor pests run counter-seasonal or year-round. Selling follows pressure because people buy when they can see the problem, which concentrates a large share of new accounts into a short window. Four consequences shape the calendar. Capacity, and any technician the operator intends to add, must be in place before the wave rather than during it, because credentialing and training take time that peak season does not have. Accounts sold early in the season receive more service events in their first year and therefore more chances to prove value before any renewal decision. Off-season selling is harder but builds the book that carries fixed cost through the slow months, and prevention-framed messaging in a quiet month must stay honest rather than manufacturing an emergency out of a season with nothing visible. And the whole pattern must be read for the specific climate zone and verified against local observation and the operator's own service history rather than imported from another region.

included: qualitative pressure waves by pest class and their effect on buying
the pre-season capacity requirement and the first-year service-event effect of sale timing
off-season book-building and honest prevention framing
verifying the pattern locally rather than importing it
excluded: selling specific seasonal add-on services and their contract mechanics
asserting emergence dates or biology as established fact for a locality
the treatment adjustments a season implies, which are the licensed operator's call

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: observed local pressure timing or the operator's service history contradicts the calendar the year was planned on

pros.claim: Treating the season as a capacity deadline rather than a sales opportunity prevents the annual cycle of overselling followed by service failure
pros.example: having the route capacity and the canvass permits in place before the first warm-weather wave instead of scrambling inside it

cons.claim: Seasonal concentration makes revenue lumpy and tempts an operator to sell whatever closes in the peak weeks regardless of route fit
cons.example: accepting scattered summer accounts far outside the zones because the phone is ringing and the season is short

failure_modes: importing another region's seasonal calendar without local verification
adding capacity during the peak instead of before it
manufacturing urgency in a quiet month to keep sales volume flat
measuring the season's success in accounts sold rather than accounts still serviced a year later
acceptance_tests: the selling calendar names the local pressure waves it is built on, the observation or service-history source for each, and the pre-season date by which capacity and permits must be in place
revisit_triggers: a season's observed pressure or demand differs from the calendar's assumption
a weather event shifts pressure timing or location
the operator's service history for the territory becomes available or is updated

nodes.definition: Govern the rate of selling by the rate at which accounts can actually be serviced, and treat the gap between the two as a managed backlog with a hard ceiling rather than as a pipeline to celebrate.
