The mechanism is direct: every sold-but-not-yet-first-serviced account has already claimed a future route slot, so when the backlog exceeds what the remaining route-days in the zone can absorb, first services slip, promised windows are missed, the promise made at the door is broken before the first invoice arrives, and cancellations land precisely inside the reversal window - which means the seller loses the commission as well as the account, and the operator loses the technician time already spent driving to a door nobody opened. The levers are all honest ones: slow the canvass, redirect selling into zones with slack, stage a portfolio's onboarding across weeks with the client's written agreement, add capacity in advance where the credentialing and training lead time allows, or hold a waitlist and tell prospects the truth about when service can begin. The rule that makes the whole thing work is simple and absolute: a start date is never promised at the door unless a slot exists to honour it.

included: the sold-not-yet-serviced backlog as a capped, measured quantity
the honest pacing levers including waitlists and staged portfolio onboarding
the rule against promising a start date without a slot
excluded: the operator's hiring, credentialing and training process
the retention conversation held with an account already in service
quoting a specific backlog limit as a universal number

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: first-service timeliness, backlog size or capacity in a zone moves against the stated ceiling

pros.claim: Capping the backlog protects the first service, which is where nearly all early cancellation is decided
pros.example: pausing canvass in a saturated zone for a fortnight so every sold account gets its first visit inside the promised window

cons.claim: Deliberately slowing sales in the middle of a short season feels like leaving money on the table and is the hardest discipline in the business to hold
cons.example: standing down a canvass team during the peak fortnight because the receiving route cannot absorb another twenty first services

failure_modes: selling to a quota while the receiving route is already saturated
promising a start date at the door that no route-day can honour
onboarding an entire portfolio in one week and missing every window in the zone
treating the backlog as a healthy pipeline rather than as consumed capacity
acceptance_tests: each zone shows its sold-not-yet-serviced backlog against remaining route-day slots, with a stated ceiling and the action taken when it is breached
no sale record contains a promised start date without a reserved slot
revisit_triggers: first-service timeliness slips in any zone
a portfolio or seasonal surge lands in one zone
capacity changes through a technician addition, loss or reassignment

nodes.definition: Maintain a small, honest scorecard per zone and use it to decide whether to keep deepening the zone or to open another. The measures that earn their place are: accounts per route-day; median stop-to-stop travel minutes, which is the most direct read on density and the first number to degrade when discipline slips; stops actually completed per day against the modelled capacity band; penetration of the target blocks; contribution per route-hour computed with the account mechanics rather than from revenue alone; early-cancellation rate by zone, which usually exposes a promise or service problem rather than a pricing one; and a standing count of outlier accounts that no route wants. The decision rule follows the shape of the curve: keep deepening while penetration is low and each marginal account shortens average travel per stop, and open new geography once added accounts inside the zone no longer improve travel per stop or the route-days are saturated. Opening deliberately resets density for a bounded period, so it is a decision taken with a stated seeding budget and an exit test written in advance, never a drift that happens because a distant lead was hard to refuse.

included: the per-zone measure set and why each is kept
the deepen-versus-open decision rule and its curve logic
the seeding budget and written exit test for opening geography
excluded: valuing the account book as an asset for sale, financing or partnership
retention interventions on individual at-risk accounts
publishing any measure as an industry benchmark figure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a zone's travel median, saturation or cancellation rate crosses the threshold that flips the deepen-or-open decision

pros.claim: A short measured scorecard makes the deepen-or-open decision routine and catches density decay long before the profit statement does
pros.example: median stop-to-stop minutes drifting upward for three weeks while account count still rises, exposing a run of outlier acceptances

cons.claim: Every measure invites gaming, and zone-level numbers can be flattered by reassigning edge accounts between zones
cons.example: moving two outliers into the neighbouring zone's list so the worked zone's travel median improves without a single route changing

failure_modes: tracking account count as the headline number and letting travel per stop degrade unseen
opening a second zone before the first can be measured at all
reading a zone's early-cancellation spike as a pricing problem when it is a promise or first-service problem
acceptance_tests: each zone reports accounts per route-day, median stop-to-stop minutes, penetration, contribution per route-hour and early-cancellation rate on a stated cadence
any decision to open new geography records its seeding budget and the exit test that ends the seeding period
revisit_triggers: median stop-to-stop travel in a zone degrades across consecutive periods
route-days in a zone reach saturation
early-cancellation rate in a zone diverges from the rest of the book

nodes.definition: Close every sale by producing the record that the licensed servicer needs and the customer can hold you to, because this is the seam where this business most often breaks. The record carries: exactly what was promised - service frequency, what is included and excluded, the re-service or guarantee arrangement as it was actually described at the door, and how billing and ending the agreement were explained at the level of mechanism; the dated, located findings evidence gathered at the property, so the technician arrives seeing what the customer was shown; the access facts that decide whether the first service succeeds at all, such as gate codes, dogs, locked side yards, whether interior access is needed and the hours the household can be present; the health, pet, pollinator and garden sensitivities elicited under the vulnerable-occupant rules, flagged for the licensed operator's judgement rather than answered by the seller; the authority basis for the contract and the name of whoever holds it; and the identity of both the seller and the operator with the written material and cancellation notice that was left. Handoff is the anti-rework gate of this entire subdomain: almost every early cancellation traces back to a gap between what a person heard at the door and what happened on the first visit, and this record is the only artifact that can close that gap before it opens.

included: the promise, findings, access, sensitivity, authority and identity contents of the handoff record
the timing rule that the record exists before the first service is scheduled
handoff as the anti-rework gate against first-visit mismatch
excluded: the service protocol the technician then designs and performs
the service agreement's own drafting, term and renewal wording
retention and cancellation-save conversations after service has begun

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: failed first services or early cancellations trace to content missing from the handoff record

pros.claim: A written promise record turns the salesman-said dispute into a document check and lets the technician deliver exactly what was sold
pros.example: a technician arriving with the gate code, the dog's name, the photographed mulch line and the note that a hive sits behind the shed

cons.claim: The record adds minutes to every close and is the first thing abandoned under peak-season pressure, precisely when it matters most
cons.example: a week of peak-season sales handed over with a phone number and an address and nothing else, followed by three failed first visits

failure_modes: handing over an address and a price with none of the promise, access or sensitivity content
recording promises that differ from what the customer's copy says
scheduling a first service before the record exists
omitting a stated sensitivity so it surfaces for the first time at the door with a technician holding equipment
acceptance_tests: no first service is scheduled without a handoff record containing promise, findings, access, sensitivity, authority and identity content
a sample of records matches the customer's own copy of what was promised, including the guarantee and ending mechanics
revisit_triggers: a first service fails for access, expectation or sensitivity reasons
an early cancellation cites something the customer believed was promised
the operator changes what it needs at handoff

edges.why_related: which model is chosen decides which revenue lines even exist for this business and whose documents prove them
commission, vesting and reversal only exist in the sell-for-operator model and are defined by the agreement the model choice selected
commission is computed on a basis drawn from the revenue lines, so the lines must be mapped before the pay mechanism can be read
the drive-time decomposition is the measurement that makes the density principle operational rather than rhetorical
zones are drawn on drive-time contours precisely because density, not distance, is what governs cost
a territory is drawn around geography that produces recurring demand, not merely around convenient roads
measured minutes per stop are the divisor that converts a working day into a stop count
capacity is computed per zone, so the zone must be defined before its capacity band can be derived
the pressure read supplies the first and heaviest criterion in the neighbourhood ranking
the home-solicitation rule classes set what must be established and disclosed before a signature is taken at a residence
the ban on invented findings is the ground the vulnerable-occupant rules stand on, since fabricated urgency does its worst damage here
identification, permitted hours, refusal handling and the cancellation notice class are inputs the conversation must obey
the conversation's persuasive content is limited to what the evidence tiers allow the seller to show and say
the stop-the-sale triggers are part of the conversation's procedure, not an exception bolted on afterwards
allocated travel minutes are a subtraction in the contribution build and come from the measured decomposition
the revenue side of the contribution build is the mapped lines at the frequency actually sold
seeding starts in the highest-ranked neighbourhood on the target list, so the ranking must exist first
the stop count a route-day can hold defines the penetration at which a seeded zone counts as open
the test asks whether a distant account still contributes, which only the contribution mechanics can answer
referral asks and warm introductions are run under the same disclosure and permission discipline as a door conversation
portfolio and association arrangements turn entirely on who holds the mandate to bind the units
triaging an inbound lead requires knowing which zone it falls in or how far outside a seam it sits
pacing decisions are made against the season's shape, since the peak is when backlog risk concentrates
contribution per route-hour on the scorecard is computed with the account mechanics rather than from revenue alone
the handoff record is the written form of exactly what the conversation promised
a canvass-based fill plan is bounded by the permit, hours, registry and private-community rules of every municipality and community the zone crosses
follow-up contact rules govern how a referred household may be telephoned, texted or emailed even when a neighbour supplied the introduction
off-season prevention messaging must stay inside the conditions tier and may never manufacture an emergency to keep volume flat
a referral must not become social pressure on a household that needs slowing down, nor disclose the referrer's own pest situation
high-intent inbound demand arrives density-blind and pushes toward accepting accounts the density test would park or refer
edges.resolution_rule: run every out-of-zone inbound lead through the same ordered test; intent may raise it to anchor status for a zone the plan already intends to open, but never exempts it from the test, and a parked lead is recorded on the named waitlist rather than quietly taken

edges.why_related: front-loaded or signature-vesting pay rewards closing pressure while the conversation discipline demands full disclosure and a clean stop at no
edges.resolution_rule: the conversation discipline wins without exception; where the pay structure rewards volume regardless of account survival, treat that as a reason to renegotiate or leave the arrangement rather than as licence to compress disclosure

edges.why_related: the peak weeks offer the year's easiest sales exactly when the receiving routes have the least slack
edges.resolution_rule: serviceable capacity wins inside the peak: sell into zones with slack, stage or waitlist the rest with an honest start date, and expand capacity only ahead of the wave, because a first service missed in peak season costs the account and the commission together

edges.why_related: a portfolio signed in one conversation can consume weeks of route slots that the capacity model had already allocated to other selling
edges.resolution_rule: accept the portfolio only with a written staged onboarding schedule that fits the receiving zone's capacity band, and pause canvass in that zone for the duration rather than letting both sources draw on the same slots

edges.why_related: rising penetration inside a fill radius shortens travel per stop, which raises the contribution of every account already on that route
promise fidelity at handoff drives whether first services succeed, and first-service failure is the dominant cause of cancellations inside the reversal window
measured conversion, travel and cancellation by zone feed back to re-rank the neighbourhood target list
first-visit failures and their recorded causes send specific corrections back into what is said and shown at the door
a zone is seeded and filled first, then measured on the scorecard, and only then compared against opening the next zone
both are warm channels that run on borrowed trust and therefore share the same disclosure duty about compensated recommendations

conflict_axes.name: route_density_versus_top_line_growth
conflict_axes.description: Every account adds revenue, but accounts outside a cluster subtract capacity and can carry negative contribution once their travel share is charged, so growth measured in account count and growth measured in route economics point different directions.
poles: take every account that will sign
take only accounts that improve or hold route density
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: judge each sale on revenue added and on its effect on travel minutes per stop in its zone; outside a cluster the ordered dilution test decides, with anchoring and scheduled absorption as the legitimate exceptions

conflict_axes.name: peak_season_harvest_versus_serviceable_capacity
conflict_axes.description: The season concentrates most of the year's easy sales into a few weeks, which is exactly when route-days have the least slack to absorb first services.
poles: sell everything the peak offers
sell only what the route can service on time
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cap the sold-not-yet-serviced backlog per zone, expand capacity ahead of the wave rather than inside it, and use honest waitlists with real start dates instead of promises the route cannot honour

conflict_axes.name: closing_pressure_versus_informed_consent
conflict_axes.description: Techniques that raise close rate at a doorstep - urgency, scarcity, social proof about neighbours, momentum through the signature - are the same techniques that produce uninformed consent and early cancellation.
poles: maximise conversion per door
maximise the share of customers who understood what they bought
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: informed consent wins absolutely; measure a canvass on accounts still serviced after several visits rather than on signatures per shift, and remove any script element that could not be replayed to the customer's family

conflict_axes.name: commission_timing_versus_account_persistence
conflict_axes.description: Pay that vests early rewards volume and pay that vests late or continues rewards durability, and a seller's behaviour follows whichever the exhibit actually specifies.
poles: optimise for commissions banked this month
optimise for accounts that survive their first year
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: read the vesting and reversal terms first and sell for persistence regardless of what the structure permits, since reversals, complaints and a closed territory cost more than any month of volume

conflict_axes.name: own_operation_control_versus_operator_partnership_leverage
conflict_axes.description: Running the licensed operation gives control of quality, price and the account book but carries cost, credentialing and liability; selling for an operator is fast and light but hands quality control, and often account ownership, to someone else.
poles: own the licence, the truck and the book
sell for an operator and carry no service cost
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decide from the agreement text rather than from preference - who owns the account, how secure the territory is, and whether the operator's service quality can be relied on - and revisit the decision whenever those clauses change

conflict_axes.name: cluster_discipline_versus_inbound_opportunism
conflict_axes.description: Inbound leads are the cheapest and highest-intent demand available and they arrive wherever they arrive, which is in direct tension with a plan that says where selling happens.
poles: work the ranked plan
follow the demand that calls you
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: spend high-intent inbound leads as anchors for zones the plan already wants, treat repeated inbound from one area as evidence to re-rank, and park or refer the isolated remainder with an honest explanation

conflict_axes.name: doorstep_brevity_versus_disclosure_completeness
conflict_axes.description: A doorstep conversation has a short natural window, but frequency, guarantee, billing, ending mechanics and the cancellation notice all have to be conveyed inside it.
poles: keep it short enough to hold attention
disclose everything material before a signature
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry the full mechanics in written leave-behind material and speak the four things a customer must be able to repeat - frequency, coverage, guarantee, how it ends - never trading disclosure for brevity

conflict_axes.name: deepen_current_zone_versus_open_new_geography
conflict_axes.description: Deepening raises density and contribution on routes that already exist; opening captures new demand but deliberately resets density and consumes selling effort at its worst return.
poles: fill the zones already open
open the next zone now
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: deepen while marginal accounts still shorten travel per stop, and open only when the scorecard shows saturation or flat travel improvement, with a stated seeding budget and a written exit test

conflict_axes.name: uniform_pricing_simplicity_versus_distance_aware_pricing
conflict_axes.description: One price across the territory is simple to sell and easy to explain, while distance-aware bands recover the travel cost that outlying accounts genuinely create.
poles: one clear price everywhere
price the distance the route actually drives
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: if a distance band exists it must be disclosed plainly at the door and justified by measured travel rather than by willingness to pay; where it cannot be explained cleanly, park or refer the account instead of hiding the cost in the price

conflict_axes.name: prevention_framing_versus_visible_problem_selling
conflict_axes.description: Recurring pest control is genuinely a prevention product, but prevention is hardest to sell in the quiet months when nothing is visible, which is precisely when invented urgency becomes tempting.
poles: sell prevention on conditions all year
sell only when the problem is visible
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep off-season messaging strictly inside the conducive-conditions tier, show the actual conditions at the property, and accept lower off-season volume rather than manufacturing a problem that is not there

edge_cases.description: A well-connected homeowner twenty-five minutes outside every open zone calls in, ready to buy today and offering to introduce neighbours later
edge_cases.trigger: a high-intent inbound lead lands far outside the served geography
edge_cases.mitigation: run the ordered test; treat the promised introductions as an anchor case only if the neighbours are contacted and confirmed before service is committed, otherwise park on the named waitlist with an honest explanation or refer to an operator already serving that area

edge_cases.description: A household that requested a quote online sits at an address carrying a posted no-soliciting sign, and the canvass team is on that street anyway
edge_cases.trigger: an inbound request collides with a do-not-knock or no-soliciting status at the same address
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the invitation as address-specific and appointment-based rather than as licence to canvass the street, confirm the appointment through the channel the household used, and record the invitation on the lead so the visit is never mistaken for cold solicitation

edge_cases.description: An elderly resident signs enthusiastically and a family member calls the next morning saying the resident does not remember the conversation
edge_cases.trigger: consent capacity is questioned after a sale has been taken
edge_cases.mitigation: cancel without argument or retention pressure, confirm the cancellation in writing, honour the jurisdiction's cancellation-notice class, and review the seller's recent sales in that neighbourhood for the same pattern

edge_cases.description: A tenant signs a recurring agreement and the landlord's management company already holds a pest-control contract for the property
edge_cases.trigger: a signature is taken from someone without authority over services at the property
edge_cases.mitigation: void the agreement, refund anything collected, approach the management company as a portfolio prospect through the proper channel, and record the reversal reason so the authority question is asked earlier in that complex

edge_cases.description: A prospect points at damaged trim and asks directly whether they have termites
edge_cases.trigger: a prospect requests a diagnosis that requires a licensed inspection
edge_cases.mitigation: state plainly that this is a licensed inspection question, describe only the visible condition without naming a cause or extent, arrange the inspection with the licensed operator, and never let the uncertainty become a closing lever

edge_cases.description: A gated community forbids solicitation entirely but a resident offers to introduce the business to several neighbours inside it
edge_cases.trigger: private community rules block canvassing in a high-density target
edge_cases.mitigation: work only through resident-initiated introductions and appointments the resident arranges, seek an association-level conversation for a sanctioned arrangement, and never enter the community to knock uninvited on the strength of one resident's welcome

edge_cases.description: A target subdivision reaches high penetration, the route-day is saturated, and the next sale on that street adds almost nothing to density
edge_cases.trigger: a zone approaches saturation while canvass momentum continues
edge_cases.mitigation: stop selling into the saturated zone, decide deliberately between adding capacity there and opening the next ranked zone with a stated seeding budget, and move the canvass rather than letting it keep working a full route

edge_cases.description: A property manager signs their whole portfolio in one meeting, adding weeks of first services to a single zone
edge_cases.trigger: a portfolio lands all at once inside one route
edge_cases.mitigation: agree a written staged onboarding schedule before signing, pause canvass in the receiving zone, and confirm start dates per property only as slots are reserved

edge_cases.description: A household discloses backyard beehives, a koi pond and a child with severe asthma while the seller is mid-conversation
edge_cases.trigger: sensitivities are raised that bear directly on how or whether service can be performed
edge_cases.mitigation: record every sensitivity verbatim, make no promise about products, methods or safety, route the questions to the licensed operator, and hold the sale until the operator confirms what can honestly be offered

edge_cases.description: Peak-season selling fills the route faster than first services can be delivered, and sold accounts wait past the promised start
edge_cases.trigger: the sold-not-yet-serviced backlog exceeds remaining route-day slots
edge_cases.mitigation: stand down or redirect canvass immediately, contact every waiting account with a real revised date before they call, prioritise first services over new sales for the period, and expect and absorb the reversals rather than disputing them

edge_cases.description: Mid-campaign it emerges that the partner operator's authority does not clearly extend to the county or service category being sold there
edge_cases.trigger: the servicing operator's licensing footprint is discovered to be unverified for a worked area
edge_cases.mitigation: stop selling in that area at once, verify the operator's current authority for the jurisdiction and category with the operator and the applicable authority, and place or refund affected accounts rather than servicing on an unverified basis

edge_cases.description: A competitor works the same subdivision the same week, undercutting on price and telling residents their neighbours have an infestation
edge_cases.trigger: a competing canvass creates price pressure and fear-based claims in a target neighbourhood
edge_cases.mitigation: hold the evidence discipline and the price mechanism, show conditions at the actual property, decline to comment on any household's situation, and let the scorecard decide whether the neighbourhood is still worth the canvass hours

workflow.action: Fix the operating model and read the agreement that defines it
workflow.description: Decide between own licensed operation and selling for a licensed operator, and extract the clauses that define territory, account ownership, compensation and termination
workflow.artifact: operating model memo with clause references
workflow.gate: who applies pesticide, who owns the account, what territory is granted, how pay is computed and what terminates it are each answered against a clause

workflow.action: Map every revenue line to its mechanism and proving document
workflow.description: Inventory initial fee, recurring fee, commission, residual and add-on lines with basis, timing, drivers and the document that proves each
workflow.artifact: revenue mechanism sheet with verification paths
workflow.gate: no line carries a figure taken from memory or hearsay, and each names the document a reader can check

workflow.action: Clear the home-solicitation regulatory screen per municipality
workflow.description: Identify permit, hours, registry, signage, private-community, cancellation-notice and follow-up contact classes for every area in the plan, with the authority consulted and the date
workflow.gate: every municipality in the canvass plan has a current dated entry with a verify-locally note, and none is older than the stated refresh cadence

workflow.action: Draw the territory boundary and its zones on drive-time contours
workflow.description: Set the outer boundary, cut zones along real barriers and drive-time contours, assign service days, and overlay municipal and community boundaries
workflow.artifact: territory and zone map with service-day assignment
workflow.gate: the map shows the outer boundary, named zones with service days, the edge-account list and every jurisdiction line a zone crosses

workflow.action: Measure drive time and decompose the cost of a stop
workflow.description: Collect real stop-to-stop travel evidence at the hours routes run and split each stop into service, travel and dead-time minutes
workflow.artifact: per-zone stop cost decomposition from route data
workflow.gate: travel minutes come from route records within the current season, not from off-peak estimates, and dead time is counted separately

workflow.description: Build stops per day from working minutes and per-stop minutes with loss adjustments, then convert to accounts supported at the sold frequency
workflow.artifact: per-zone capacity band with written assumptions
workflow.gate: the band lists its working-minute, per-stop and loss assumptions and derives accounts supported at the frequency actually sold

workflow.action: Read pest pressure and rank the target neighbourhoods
workflow.description: Walk candidate areas, record the habitat and structural drivers, then rank on pressure, homogeneity, owner-occupancy, doors per mile, access class, competitor saturation and distance from a cluster
workflow.artifact: ranked neighbourhood target list with written reasons
workflow.gate: each entry states a reason built only from pest, property, access and route facts, with no protected-characteristic or demographic proxy criterion

workflow.action: Set the evidence and consent standard before anyone knocks
workflow.description: Write the three-tier evidence rule, the recording requirement, the referral rule for licensed-opinion questions, and the stop-the-sale triggers for consent and sensitivity
workflow.artifact: selling conduct standard with scripts and leave-behind material
workflow.gate: no script contains urgency, fear, fabricated social proof or a diagnostic claim, and every script requires a shown, dated observation

workflow.action: Seed the first zone with an anchor and fill concentrically
workflow.description: Secure an anchor account or portfolio, then concentrate all canvass and referral effort inside the smallest walkable radius until penetration supports a route
workflow.artifact: zone seeding plan with anchor, fill radius and penetration target
workflow.gate: only one zone is in seeding, its anchor and fill radius are named, and the penetration level that ends seeding is written down in advance

workflow.action: Run the door, referral and partner channels under the conduct standard
workflow.description: Work the ranked list with identification, disclosure, permission, shown findings, plain mechanics and written leave-behind, taking referrals as warm introductions
workflow.artifact: contact and sale log with consent, authority and findings evidence
workflow.gate: every contact record shows identification given, material left, authority established and at least one dated observation, and no contact continued after a refusal

workflow.action: Score density per zone and decide deepen or open
workflow.description: Report accounts per route-day, median stop-to-stop minutes, penetration, contribution per route-hour and early cancellations, apply the dilution test to outliers, and check the sold-not-yet-serviced backlog against remaining slots
workflow.artifact: per-zone density scorecard with a deepen-or-open decision and backlog position
workflow.gate: the backlog sits inside its ceiling, every outlier account carries a recorded decision, and any decision to open new geography states its seeding budget and exit test

workflow.action: Complete the promise record and hand the account to the licensed servicer
workflow.description: Assemble promise, findings, access, sensitivity, authority and identity content and transfer it before any first service is scheduled
workflow.gate: no first service is scheduled without a complete record, and a sample reconciles against the customer's own copy of what was promised

priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because nothing downstream is decidable without them: the operating model fixes who owns the account and who may apply anything, the revenue and commission mechanisms fix how a dollar comes to exist, and the home-solicitation screen fixes where a door may be knocked at all; the density principle, measured drive time, territory geometry and route-day capacity then build the cost and capacity frame that every later decision is judged against; pressure reading and neighbourhood ranking convert that frame into a target list, and the evidence, consent and authority nodes must exist before any of it is walked, because they constrain the conversation rather than decorate it; the channel nodes, the dilution test and seeding then execute against those constraints; and the seasonal calendar, pacing, scorecard and promise-record handoff come last because each composes the earlier work into a measured, serviceable, honestly documented book of accounts.

dominance_rules.rule: Licensed-application reality dominates every selling opportunity
dominance_rules.rationale: pesticide application is credentialed work and an account sold outside the servicing operator's authorised jurisdiction or category cannot be lawfully or safely delivered
dominance_rules.trigger: a prospect sits outside the verified area or asks for a service class the operator's authority does not clearly cover
dominance_rules.action: stop selling there, verify the operator's current authority with the operator and the applicable authority, and decline or refer until it is confirmed

dominance_rules.rule: Home-solicitation rules dominate the canvass plan
dominance_rules.rationale: permits, hours, do-not-knock registries, posted signage and private community rules bind regardless of how attractive a street is
dominance_rules.trigger: a planned route touches an unscreened municipality, a listed address, a posted sign or a community that forbids solicitation
dominance_rules.action: remove the address or area from the plan and work it only through invited, appointment-based or association-sanctioned contact

dominance_rules.rationale: invented findings and manufactured urgency produce cancellations, complaints and a reputation that closes a territory permanently
dominance_rules.trigger: a claim is about to be made that nothing observed at this property supports
dominance_rules.action: drop the claim, show only what is there, and refer any diagnostic question to a licensed inspection

dominance_rules.rationale: a signature from someone who cannot recall or understand the conversation is worth nothing and harms a household
dominance_rules.trigger: capacity, comprehension or language raises any doubt at the door
dominance_rules.action: stop the sale, leave written information and identification, and offer to return when a family member, carer or interpreter is present

dominance_rules.rule: Authority to contract dominates a willing signature
dominance_rules.rationale: an account signed by someone without authority over services at the property cancels early and can leave a household paying twice
dominance_rules.trigger: ownership, tenancy, management mandate or existing coverage is unclear
dominance_rules.action: obtain written confirmation from the party who holds authority before any service is scheduled

dominance_rules.rule: Route density dominates raw account count when the two conflict
dominance_rules.rationale: an account that lowers contribution per route-hour is not growth however good it looks on a sales report
dominance_rules.trigger: a prospective account falls outside an existing or planned cluster
dominance_rules.action: apply the ordered dilution test and record the accept, absorb, price, park or refer decision with its reason

dominance_rules.rule: Serviceable capacity dominates sales pace, most absolutely in peak season
dominance_rules.rationale: a missed or late first service breaks the doorstep promise before the first invoice and costs the account and the commission together
dominance_rules.trigger: the sold-not-yet-serviced backlog in a zone approaches the remaining route-day slots
dominance_rules.action: stand down or redirect canvass, stage portfolio onboarding, and give waiting customers a real revised start date before they have to ask

dominance_rules.rationale: reversals, complaints and lost referral flow outlast any month of front-loaded volume
dominance_rules.trigger: the pay structure would reward a sale the seller does not expect to survive its first services
dominance_rules.action: decline the sale and treat a structure that rewards volume regardless of survival as a reason to renegotiate or exit the arrangement

dominance_rules.rule: The written promise record dominates rapport and speed at handoff
dominance_rules.rationale: almost every early cancellation traces to a gap between what was heard at the door and what happened on the first visit
dominance_rules.trigger: a sale is about to be passed to the servicing operator without complete promise, access, sensitivity and authority content
dominance_rules.action: hold the scheduling until the record is complete rather than letting the technician discover the gap at the property

dominance_rules.rule: Verified mechanism dominates any quoted figure
dominance_rules.rationale: prices, commissions, clawback windows and account values differ by operator, territory and season, and an invented number becomes a promise nobody can keep
dominance_rules.trigger: a price, commission, payback or account-value number is about to be stated to a customer, partner or recruit
dominance_rules.action: state the mechanism and its drivers, then verify the actual figure against the current document for that specific deal

anti_rework_rules.rule: Clear the per-municipality solicitation screen before building any canvass plan for that area
anti_rework_rules.prevents: scrapping a completed schedule, permit exposure and citations discovered in the middle of a campaign

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the servicing operator's authority for the jurisdiction and service category before selling into new geography
anti_rework_rules.prevents: sold accounts that cannot be lawfully serviced and must be refunded, reassigned or cancelled

anti_rework_rules.rule: Draw the territory geometry and assign service days before any canvassing starts
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a scattered early book that no routing can ever make profitable and that must be shed account by account

anti_rework_rules.rule: Measure real stop-to-stop travel before pricing distance or promising service windows
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a price and window model built on off-peak estimates that has to be rebuilt after the first season

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read and write down the compensation, vesting and clawback mechanism before running a volume push
anti_rework_rules.prevents: pay disputes, budgeting on commissions that reverse, and selling the accounts the structure quietly punishes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture dated findings evidence at the moment of sale, not afterwards from memory
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unresolvable he-said disputes, technician arrivals that contradict the sale, and cancellations that cannot be defended

anti_rework_rules.rule: Establish authority to contract before taking a signature
anti_rework_rules.prevents: landlord and management cancellations, duplicate coverage for a household, and reversals inside the clawback window

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record access facts and household sensitivities during the sale conversation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: failed first services at locked gates and with unrestrained dogs, and safety questions surfacing when a technician is already on site

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pace against capacity before the season's peak rather than during it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a peak-season cancellation wave caused by late first services, and the reversals that arrive with it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Baseline the density scorecard for a zone before opening the next one
anti_rework_rules.prevents: opening geography that cannot be compared or measured, and discovering only later which zone was carrying the losses

iteration_protocol.trigger: median stop-to-stop travel minutes in a zone degrade across consecutive reporting periods
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the dilution test on the zone's outlier accounts, re-cluster the service days, and pause selling outside the fill radius until the median recovers

iteration_protocol.trigger: early cancellations cluster in one zone or one seller's accounts
iteration_protocol.action: audit the handoff records and first-service timeliness for those accounts before touching price, and retrain on whatever the doorstep conversation actually promised

iteration_protocol.trigger: a municipality enacts or amends a solicitation ordinance, registry or consumer-cancellation requirement, or the plan extends into an unscreened area
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the regulatory screen for that area, refresh the checklist entry with its date and authority, and hold the canvass until it is current

iteration_protocol.trigger: the partner operator's authority, territory grant, compensation exhibit or account-ownership terms change
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the agreement, re-derive the revenue and commission mechanisms, and re-test whether the operating model still holds

iteration_protocol.trigger: a season turns or observed pressure diverges from the selling calendar
iteration_protocol.action: re-rank the target neighbourhoods for the new pressure class, adjust message framing inside the evidence tiers, and re-pace selling against remaining capacity

iteration_protocol.trigger: land use changes inside the territory through new construction, clearing, a water feature or a demolished habitat
iteration_protocol.action: re-walk the affected micro-geography, update the pressure drivers on record, and reconsider whether the area justifies seeding or re-ranking

iteration_protocol.trigger: a complaint, review or family contact alleges pressure, an invented finding or a consent problem at the door
iteration_protocol.action: pull the sale record and its evidence, cancel and refund where the allegation holds, retrain on the specific script element involved, and audit that seller's recent accounts in the same neighbourhood

iteration_protocol.trigger: inbound lead volume from an unopened area crosses the level that would justify an anchor
iteration_protocol.action: re-rank that area against the target list, convert the strongest inbound accounts into anchors, and open the zone with a stated seeding budget and exit test
